newsitem.title: HUNGARY: THAI BAHT CRISIS DOES NOT AFFECT HUNGARY - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: THAI BAHT CRISIS DOES NOT AFFECT HUNGARY - C.BANK.

text.p: Hungary's forint will be unaffected by a plunge of the currency of Thailand, another emerging market economy, National Bank of Hungary President Gyorgy Suranyi said a news conference.
"(Thai financial difficulties) nor other events which happened in a closer area (the Czech Republic) could affect Hungary," Suranyi said, answering a journalist's question.

The Thai baht plunged 15-20 percent on off-shore markets, tempting the government to take tough measures to help the economy grappling with a swollen current account deficit and a troubled financial sector.
Suranyi said a financial crisis in an emerging economy can affect other such economies under special circumstances even if they are geographically far from each other.
But Hungary's current position was very different from its situation at the turn of 1994 and 1995, when the financial crisis in Mexico weighed heavily on the Hungarian economy, Suranyi said.

Soaring budget and current account deficits and foreign currency deposit withdrawals compelled Hungary to introduce a strict austerity package in March 1995 but the economy has stabilised and was on track towards a sustainable growth, he said.
However, Suranyi added that according to his information, the impact of the Thai economic difficulties contributed to the currency crisis which the Czech Republic went through earlier this year.
